summary: Git LFS authentication failures on ephemeral runners during KMS rewrap causing large-file uploads to fail
description: Summary: After a scheduled bulk KMS rewrap of several secrets (2026-03-10 01:30 UTC), multiple ephemeral CI runners started failing Git LFS operations when performing release jobs that fetch/push large artifacts. The failures were intermittent and correlated with secret propagation windows. Impact: blocking canary and rollouts for two services that rely on Git LFS assets; observed ~30% of release jobs failing with LFS auth errors between 01:35-02:20 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a release job on an ephemeral runner that clones a repo with Git LFS-tracked files (~100-500MB objects).
2) During or immediately after our KMS rewrap window, let the job reach the git-lfs fetch/pull phase (smudge).
3) Observe the git-lfs helper attempting to fetch objects and failing with 401/403 despite kubernetes secrets being updated in Vault and mounted into the runner pod.
4) Repeatable on multiple ephemeral runners but not observed on dedicated machines where tokens are long-lived.
observed_behavior: Git LFS operations fail with authentication errors. Example log lines: 'git-lfs: HTTP 401 Unauthorized', 'fatal: Authentication failed for "https://git.internal.company/repo.git/"', and 'PostBuffer overflow / unexpected EOF during object download'. Runners show valid secret mounts but internal credential helper (git-credential-cache / lfs helper) still using old token leading to failed requests to storage backend.
expected_behavior: Runners should seamlessly pick up new credentials after secret rewrap and Git LFS fetches should succeed without requiring runner restart or manual cache invalidation.
logs: [runner-abc-123] 2026-03-10T01:36:12Z credential-helper: cached credentials lookup returned token with expiry 2026-03-10T01:40:01Z (old epoch)
investigation_notes: Timeline: KMS rewrap completed at ~01:33 UTC. Secret controller applied new Kubernetes secret versions at ~01:34 UTC. Failures started at 01:35 UTC and persisted for certain runners until we restarted their pods.

Hypothesis: Git credential helper or LFS helper caches tokens in-memory or in an on-disk credential cache and does not react to Kubernetes secret file updates. The new token's short TTL and our rewrap/grace-window overlap caused some helpers to keep using the stale token until either cache TTL expired or runner restarted.

Reproduced locally by simulating secret file rotate: replacing mounted file with new token without restarting git-credential-cache process — observed helper continued returning old token until helper service restarted.

Observed difference between dedicated vs ephemeral: dedicated runners run long-lived agents that proactively refresh tokens via token-manager service; ephemeral runners rely on a short-lived credential helper bundled in runner image which caches credentials per process.
Checked related systems: secrets-controller logs show successful write; kubelet mount events show file update timestamp changed as expected. No errors in Vault rewrap itself.

Potential contributing factor: token TTL was 5m with a 1m grace window; propagation lag across kubelets in us-east reached up to ~60s during the bulk rotate event. Where kubelet mounted new secret but the helper process still held older token epoch, causing 401s against storage which enforces epoch-checking.
Links: Slack thread #release-ops (https://slack.redwood/#release-ops) and runbook 'CI Runner Token Rotation' (https://confluence.redwood/ci/token-rotation-runbook)

Related existing ticket: INT-531807 (runner-credential-refresh-stalemate-during-multi-region-key-roll) — similar but multi-region; this is specifically LFS object flow and credential-helper caching behavior.
root_cause: Credential helper caching on ephemeral runners didn't invalidate cached tokens on file-based secret updates. Combined with short-lived tokens from the KMS rewrap and token epoch enforcement on the storage backend, some runners attempted LFS fetches with stale tokens causing 401s.
workaround: Temporary mitigation applied: updated release jobs to set GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 to avoid immediate LFS fetch during clone, then performed a manual 'git lfs pull' after a small sleep + CLI invocation that restarts the credential helper. Also restarted affected ephemeral runner pods to force helper process restart. This allowed canary promotions to proceed.
resolution: In progress: patch merged to secrets-controller to emit a token rotation lifecycle hook that notifies the runner agent (via pod annotation) to restart the git-credential-helper process. Patch: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/secrets-controller/pull/1423. Additionally, the token-manager has been reconfigured to extend the rewrap grace window from 60s -> 180s for Git LFS tokens. Deployment: secrets-controller v2.8.1 was rolled to us-east on 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC; token-manager config updated at 2026-03-12 03:05 UTC. Monitoring: rolling check completed across 120 ephemeral runner nodes; post-deploy failures fell to 0.5% and then to 0% after finishing cache invalidation rollout.
next_steps: 1) Backport secrets-controller lifecycle hook to stable release channel (PR queued).
2) Add unit/integration test that simulates file-based secret swap and asserts credential helper revalidation.
3) Update the runbook with explicit guidance for Git LFS-heavy repositories (include GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE option).
4) Review token TTLs for other short-lived helpers used by ephemeral runners and increase grace windows where safe.
5) Postmortem to be drafted if customer-facing rollouts were delayed beyond SLA thresholds.
